data.summary: An older ddflow reading the primary's newer .ddflow/config.toml refuses every command: once 1bdefdf added [worktree].local_files to the committed config, running ddflow in any worktree whose code predates it (the tree's own ddflow package is imported from cwd, while config is read from the PRIMARY checkout) fails with ValueError: unknown knob 'worktree.local_files', including the harness trees of live parallel sessions and MCP servers started in them. Repro: cd .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01C1TEJNQxh6UgFfDYxifnmU (code at 5e847a6); ddflow status -> ValueError. Same class as B8ea7a90aea (primary config vs tree code). Fix direction: an unknown knob from a newer config is a warning naming the knob and 'merge main', not a crash; or read config from the tree whose code runs.

data.how: for p in $(pgrep -f 'kilo run --format json'); do [ "$(ps -o ppid= -p $p | tr -d ' ')" = 1 ] && kill $p; done. Prefer one review at a time per LAN endpoint; wrapping roborev in 'timeout' kills the node launcher but not the .kilo child.
data.rule: After any kilo-backed review times out or is cancelled, reap orphaned '.kilo run' processes (ppid 1) before starting another review
data.title: A timed-out kilo review leaves its native .kilo child running and saturates the shared LAN reviewer
data.why: 2026-09-29: 18 orphaned '.kilo run --model lanqwen/...' processes (ppid 1, 30 min to 2.5 h old) were still querying the LAN Qwen endpoint after their roborev/timeout parents exited; with 7 concurrent ddflow review runs this made every critic time out at 3600 s or come back off-contract.

data.how: for p in $(pgrep -f 'kilo run --format json'); do [ "$(ps -o ppid= -p $p | tr -d ' ')" = 1 ] && kill $p; done -- or restart the roborev daemon; the durable fix belongs in roborev/kilo (kill the process group).
data.rule: Before and during long review work, reap orphaned '.kilo run' processes (ppid 1); run one review at a time per LAN endpoint
data.title: The roborev daemon leaks a .kilo process per review, which saturates the shared LAN reviewer
data.why: 2026-09-29: the roborev daemon (roborev daemon run) spawns 'node kilo run' -> '.kilo run' per job; when the job ends the node launcher exits and the native .kilo child is re-parented to init and keeps querying the LAN endpoint. 18 were reaped at one point, 9 more an hour later; with them live every ddflow critic timed out at 3600 s or came back off-contract. Wrapping roborev in 'timeout' leaks the same way.

data.how: Set temperature = 1.0 on the [[reviewer]] in .ddflow/reviewers.toml. To diagnose, wrap services.review._open and dump choices[0].message.reasoning_content's tail.
data.rule: Run reasoning-model reviewers at the vendor's recommended temperature (DeepSeek: 1.0), not ddflow's 0.3 default; before blaming chunk size or reasoning_effort, read the reasoning tail
data.title: A reasoning-model reviewer at low temperature loops until its token budget is gone
data.why: 2026-09-29: lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash at temperature 0.3 truncated chunk 1 of 223d493 at 64000 reasoning tokens on every reasoning_effort tried (low, high, 25; top-level and chat_template_kwargs); the reasoning tail was 'OK, NO FINDINGS. ... let me reconsider' repeated. At 1.0 the same diff reviewed fully in 419 s. thinking=false finished in 121 s but reported clean where a thinking run found issues.

data.body: Operator 2026-09-29: 'Implement ddflow command to close a bug as invalid / false finding' -- B97355c6d15 (B-wait-wake critic: cap-blocked item refused as hopeless) was shown false by a test, but the only way to close a bug is 'bug fixed', which claims a fix and a regression test that fails on the unfixed code; there is none, so it stays open forever and inflates the open-bug count. Scope: (a) event bug.invalid {reason, evidence}; fold: Bug gains invalid_at/invalid_reason/evidence and a resolution ('fixed'|'invalid'), open = neither; a later bug.found re-merges, never reopens silently; (b) api bug_invalid(id, reason, evidence): refuse (exit 3) an unknown id (same hint as bug_fixed), an already fixed/invalid bug, an empty reason; evidence = a probe command or test node id, resolved statically like bug fixed's --regression-test when it names a test; (c) CLI 'ddflow bug invalid <id> --reason ... [--evidence ...]' + MCP ddflow_bug_invalid, parity-tested; (d) every reader of Bug.open / fixed_at (status open-bug count, brief, recall BUG '[fixed]' label, replay/render reconstruction, progress) shows 'invalid: <reason>' distinctly from fixed -- a false finding is not a fix and must never count toward 'bugs fixed'. Surface wiring (cli.py, mcp.py, api/__init__.py, help.py, test_mcp_parity.py, test_api_layer.py) is held by B-precommit-companion: widen globs once it releases. Regression tests: close-as-invalid on an open bug -> not open, not counted fixed, reason shown; unknown id and fixed bug refused exit 3; empty reason refused. Then close B97355c6d15 with it.
data.title: ddflow bug invalid: close a recorded bug as a false finding, with a reason and a probe, never as fixed

data.alternatives: Block complete on a failed critic until a re-review passes: rejected -- forces open-ended re-review of fixed findings. Require re-recording critic after fixes: rejected for the same reason.
data.consequences: The critic's findings are advisory at completion: whoever completes must have triaged them (fixed with a failing-first test, or filed as bugs). A stale 'failed' can sit on a completed item, so read the evidence and the bugs, not the mark, when auditing.
data.context: Operator 2026-09-30: 'Do not block' -- asked about B-fix-bug-fixed-refuses-unknown (b71d55e), which completed with critic 'failed' from an earlier DeepSeek pass whose findings were all fixed with regression tests afterwards; re-reviewing until a pass comes back clean had become an unbounded loop (five full passes, each finding a new edge case).
data.decision: complete accepts an item whose critic gate is recorded 'failed'. 'failed' is an outcome like any other: the every-gate-has-an-outcome rule is satisfied, and the reviewer-independence rule (a different-family review on record) still applies. Do not add a complete-time refusal for a failed critic.
data.title: A failed critic outcome does not block ddflow complete

data.body: Bug B9cb7dd1c3b: a worktree nested under the primary (.claude/worktrees/*, .kilo/worktrees/*) imports ITS OWN ddflow code but reads the PRIMARY's .ddflow/config.toml; config.py:1186 raises ValueError('unknown knob ...') on any knob newer than the tree's code, so every command fails there (12 harness trees broken by enforce.forbidden_trailers; local_files would have broken 3 more -> disabled in d52d472). Operator 2026-09-30 agreed: keep local_files off until this is fixed, then turn it back on. Research first: why that code/config pairing (cwd import vs config discovery), and whether the right fix is (a) an unknown knob in a known section is a warning naming the knob and 'your ddflow is older than this config: merge main' (a typo'd knob must still be caught -- e.g. refuse when the SAME code's own templates/docs do not know it, or keep refusing in the primary/--strict), and/or (b) reading config from the tree whose code runs. Mind decision/lesson on silent-knob-drop: never silently ignore. Sibling: B-fix-gate-config-drift (bug B8ea7a90aea, services/gates.py) is the same primary-config-vs-tree-code class for gate commands -- do not take its scope. Regression test: config with a knob the code does not know -> commands still run and name the knob (fails on current code with ValueError); a typo'd knob is still reported. Last step: uncomment local_files = ['.roborev.toml'] in .ddflow/config.toml (d52d472's note) and verify an older nested harness tree (e.g. .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01PsvUbFf1s1M5qBj52UYuhg) still runs 'ddflow status'.
data.title: An older ddflow reading a newer .ddflow/config.toml warns on an unknown knob instead of refusing every command; then re-enable [worktree].local_files (fixes bug B9cb7dd1c3b)

data.claim: Yes via the existing copilot target (MCP .github/mcp.json, AGENTS.md, github-copilot delta), but completion fails reviewer independence: an author model named 'hydrafusion' resolves to no family, and HydraFusion mixes families per task so no single author family exists
data.falsifier: family_for('hydrafusion') returns a family, or Copilot CLI with HydraFusion cannot call MCP tools
data.probe: family_of() over 'hydrafusion','HydraFusion','copilot/hydrafusion' with this repo's Config; read github.blog HydraFusion post
data.probe_output: all three -> '' (unrecognised); post: CLI-only research preview via /experimental, selected like a model, patterns single/cascade/critique (critique uses a different-family reviewer, tool-less), best on first-turn single-prompt tasks, multi-turn still in development; no mention of MCP/AGENTS.md
data.question: Can ddflow drive an agent that runs GitHub Copilot CLI's HydraFusion multi-model mode?

data.body: Operator 2026-10-01 asked whether ddflow can work with GitHub Copilot CLI's Project HydraFusion (research R7dbec5e53a, https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/project-hydrafusion-frontier-quality-via-multi-model-orchestration/). It can drive it through the existing copilot target, but: family_for('hydrafusion') == '' so complete refuses ('author's model is not in [agent].families'), and HydraFusion picks models across providers per task (single / cascade / critique), so no single author family exists; its internal different-family critique is invisible to ddflow and is not gate evidence. Scope: (a) [agent].routers (or a families value that is a list): a model name that maps to a SET of families, shipped default hydrafusion -> the providers the post names (research which, CONFIRMED with sources; unknown members recorded as such); (b) reviewer_independence: an author that is a set is independent of a reviewer only if the reviewer's family is outside the WHOLE set; a router author with an unknown member set is never assumed independent -- the refusal names the knob to set; (c) complete/merge --model hydrafusion then works with this repo's DeepSeek reviewer iff deepseek is outside the set; (d) github-copilot delta: HydraFusion is strongest on first-turn single-prompt tasks (per the post), so drive it per step -- claim, then one HydraFusion turn for implement, then ddflow gates -- not the whole loop in one conversation; its internal critique does not replace rubber_duck/critic. Regression tests: hydrafusion author + deepseek reviewer -> independent; + a reviewer in the set -> refused naming the overlap; an unconfigured router -> refused with the knob named; a plain single-family author unchanged. Fails on current code.
data.title: A router author (Copilot HydraFusion) is a SET of families: independence needs a reviewer outside all of them; the Copilot delta says to drive it per step
